newsitem.title: USA: Minister sees further cuts in India fiscal deficit.
newsitem.headline: Minister sees further cuts in India fiscal deficit.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister Palaniappan Chidambaram said Wednesday his country hoped to cut its fiscal deficit to 4.0 percent of gross domestic product over the next two or three years from the 5.0 percent projected in the current budget.
In remarks before the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Chidambaram said he expected growth this year of 6.5 percent, a "replication of the last two years."
He told the group that India needed $150 billion over the next five years "in order to build a world class infrastructure."
He said the country could presently absorb $10 billion a year in foreign direct investment as long as the funding was used primarily for the country's infrastructure.
He also said the country was committed to tariff reform --currently at 27 percent -- and had as a goal to bring it down to Asian averages by the end of decade and to world levels a few years later.
Chidambaram is in Washington to attend the annual International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings.
